title: Found, but Not Fixed : From Software Vulnerability Discovery to Fixes with Iterative LLM Pipelines
abstract: arXiv:2611.19719v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Software vulnerabilities persist as a critical threat despite the deployment of sophisticated detection tools and AI assistants. While detection has advanced, the subsequent code repair phase remains a primary bottleneck; manual intervention is inherently slow, costly, and prone to introducing secondary regressions and issues. In this paper, we investigate whether an iterative, LLM-based pipeline can provide a robust solution for the automated repair of vulnerable functions in real-world code. We propose a generalized framework that leverages the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) through a multi-stage feedback loop. We benchmark this approach against state-of-the-art models, including GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, and Gemini 3 Flash, demonstrating that such a pipeline can achieve high-quality code repair. translated_title: 发现但未修复：使用迭代式LLM流水线从软件漏洞发现到修复
translated_abstract: 尽管已经部署了先进的检测工具和AI助手，软件漏洞仍然是一个严重的威胁。虽然检测技术已取得进展，但随后的代码修复阶段仍然是主要瓶颈；人工干预本质上缓慢、成本高昂，并且容易引入二次回归和问题。在本文中，我们研究了基于LLM的迭代流水线能否为真实世界代码中易受攻击函数的自动化修复提供稳健的解决方案。我们提出了一个通用框架，通过多阶段反馈循环利用大型语言模型（LLM）的推理能力。我们将该方法与最先进的模型（包括GPT-4o、GPT-5.1和Gemini 3 Flash）进行基准测试，证明这样的流水线能够实现高质量的代码修复。为支持更广泛的安全社区，我们提供了评估框架、微调权重和全面的实验结果。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于LLM迭代流水线的通用框架，通过多阶段反馈循环实现真实世界代码中漏洞函数的自动化高质量修复，并在GPT-4o、GPT-5.1和Gemini 3 Flash等最先进模型上验证了其有效性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a generalized iterative LLM-based pipeline with multi-stage feedback loops that achieves high-quality automated repair of vulnerable functions in real-world code, benchmarked against state-of-the-art models including GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, and Gemini 3 Flash.
